I grant no business, Finance or IT approval. Product gate G6 is not engineering gate DG7.

checks_run.procedure: Verify F-DG1-010, which I raised in round 8. The testkit header and the governing decision must no longer base an exhaustiveness claim on a specific (wrong) Node version. Any Node version the header still names must match the repository's pins. The lint's correctness must no longer depend on Node 24 vs Node 22.
checks_run.command: grep -n -i 'node 2[0-9]|22\.|24|exhaustive|closed as found|pinned' apps/api/src/architecture.testkit.ts; cat .nvmrc; grep engines package.json; grep NODE_IMAGE deploy/docker/Dockerfile; grep 'Target runtime|floor' ADR-0001; D-055 row in docs/delivery/decisions.md; read the SAFE_NODE_BUILTINS / SAFE_PROCESS_MEMBERS / bareAllowed / rule-3 code
checks_run.environment: repository at HEAD 07f1a54 (candidate tree identical to 273d21f)
checks_run.expected: no 'exhaustive for the pinned Node 22' wording; any version named is factual (Node 24 target, 22.18+ floor); built-in and process checks are allow-lists, not version-specific enumerations
checks_run.actual: The header no longer contains 'exhaustive', 'closed as found' or 'pinned'. Its single version mention (line 42) is factual context: 'production targets Node 24, the supported floor is Node 22.18+'. That matches .nvmrc=24, engines '>=22.18.0 <25', the Dockerfile node:24 image and ADR-0001 (target 24 LTS, floor 22.18.0). The claim is now structural: bareAllowed returns SAFE_NODE_BUILTINS.has(name) for every node: specifier, and rule 3 flags any process.<member> outside SAFE_PROCESS_MEMBERS. A built-in or member that any Node version adds is therefore denied without a per-version sweep. My own negative control confirms it: 'node:some-future-builtin' is denied. D-055 explicitly supersedes the D-053/D-054 'closed as found / exhaustive for the pinned Node' framing. D-054 stays as a superseded historical row, which is correct for an append-only log. Limitation, stated honestly: this sandbox has only Node 20/21/22 and no network, so I did not execute the lint on Node 24. That is not needed to verify this finding, because the fixed claim no longer depends on the runtime version.

checks_run.procedure: Run the architecture suite verbose. This covers the ADR-0002 module boundaries, the real module tree, and the default-deny positive and negative self-checks.

Run an independent over-reach probe written by me. (1) moduleViolations is zero for every module. (2) An AST inventory written separately from the testkit scanner lists every node: specifier and process.<member> in src/modules/**, and each must be allow-listed. (3) Positive controls: ordinary module code (node:crypto randomUUID, node:fs/promises, node:url+node:path, node:util+node:os, process.env, process.argv/once/exit, decimal.js) must give no violations. (4) Negative controls: process.kill / _debugProcess / getBuiltinModule / execve / dlopen, and node:inspector, inspector/promises, wasi, v8, net, http, test/reporters, sqlite, a hypothetical future built-in and a bare 'fs' must each give a violation.
checks_run.command: cp 03-default-deny-overreach-probe.test.ts apps/api/src/zz-dom-r9-probe.test.ts (clone only); npx vitest run --project unit-node apps/api/src/zz-dom-r9-probe.test.ts --reporter=verbose
checks_run.environment: disposable clone at 273d21f; the probe file was never in the candidate tree and was removed from the clone before the build
checks_run.expected: 4/4 pass; inventory ⊆ allow-lists; positive controls []; every negative control ≥1 violation
checks_run.actual: 4 passed (4), exit 0. Inventory: node:crypto x5, node:path x3, node:fs x1, node:url x1. Module source uses no process.<member> at all. All seven positive controls give []. All 15 negative controls are denied, with messages such as 'non-allow-listed process._debugProcess member' and 'imports non-allow-listed node built-in node:inspector'. So no legitimate import or member in the real tree is rejected. One observation, not a defect: harmless read-only members such as process.pid, and built-ins such as node:events, are now also denied. No module uses them, and D-055's reopen criterion (review, then add deliberately) covers future needs.
